method: Read the complete WorkerClient transport and current diff; traced actual connection/beforeWrite boundary, response parsing/capacity, error metadata whitelist and unknown classification.

Read Dispatcher mutation admission/dispatch/settlement/replay and unchanged Ledger reserve/digest/settle/read code, receipt-result and HarnessError projection. Read the new gateway fixture cases plus existing file-backed partial-receipt restart/replay cases.

Read requireHistoryConversionConsent and its turn/start and cold thread/resume call sites for source/target binding and pre-mutation use. This is a narrow independent gateway-contract review, not an independent audit of my own frontend consent authoring or the separate native helper implementation.
conclusions: Confirmation metadata is projected only for the exact confirmation-required code with not_sent delivery and conversionRequired true. Four primitive bounded fields survive; unrelated/private history fields are discarded. Unknown conversion errors do not get the confirmation metadata.

Dispatcher forwards the top-level consent object in params unchanged to the worker. Ledger reserve hashes the complete method/params and binds thread scope, so changing consent while reusing an operation ID is a conflict rather than a new dispatch.

An existing receipt returns before current worker admission. not_sent replay now preserves both explicit delivery and saved data; pending/unknown replay is still unknown, with no second worker call. New explicit user approval must use a different operation ID.

Ledger settle persists error.data as bounded JSON atomically; read reconstructs terminal delivery from the durable state. On reopening the journal terminal not_sent is not rewritten into pending, and replay does not call the worker. Capacity failures remain conservative.

Runtime consent accepts exactly two fields and checks each provider against the actual current transition, including same-provider repair. Stale source/target is not_sent. Omitted consent is accepted only when the runtime determines conversion is not required.

All added fields are consumed: the frontend uses matching thread/provider metadata to show confirmation; the runtime consumes top-level consent before conversion; saved receipt data supports identical original-ID replay. Consent is not saved as model settings.
